title: Dishonour of Cheque (Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881)
statutory_prerequisites: Cheque presented to bank within validity period (3 months from issuance date)
Cheque returned unpaid with official bank return memo stating 'Insufficient Funds' or exceeding arranged amount
Notice demand must be for the exact cheque amount or legally enforceable debt

procedural_steps.title: Obtain Official Bank Return Memo
procedural_steps.description: Secure the original bounced cheque along with the stamped Bank Return Memo stating the specific reason for dishonour.
evidence_required: Stamped Bank Return Memo with date and cheque return code

procedural_steps.title: Serve Statutory Legal Demand Notice
procedural_steps.statutory_deadline: Strictly within 30 days of receiving the bank memo
procedural_steps.description: Issue a formal demand notice to the drawer demanding payment of the cheque amount. Must be sent via Registered Post with A/D, Speed Post, or verifiable email/WhatsApp.
evidence_required: Copy of Legal Demand Notice signed by complainant/advocate
India Post online delivery tracking report showing delivery/refusal

procedural_steps.title: Wait for 15-Day Statutory Cure Period
procedural_steps.statutory_deadline: 15 days from date of receipt of notice by drawer
procedural_steps.description: The drawer is granted a statutory window of 15 days to make payment. No criminal complaint can be filed before this 15-day period expires.
evidence_required: Proof of service date (India Post tracking or postal acknowledgment card)

procedural_steps.title: File Criminal Complaint before Judicial Magistrate
procedural_steps.statutory_deadline: Within 30 days starting on Day 16 after notice receipt
procedural_steps.description: If payment is not made within 15 days, cause of action arises on Day 16. File a criminal complaint under Section 138/142 before the Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate in whose jurisdiction the payee bank account is located.
evidence_required: Affidavit of evidence under Section 145 NI Act

statutory_relief: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both; plus interim compensation up to 20% under Section 143A.
forum: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate Court

title: Consumer Deficiency & Unfair Trade Practice (Consumer Protection Act, 2019)
statutory_prerequisites: Goods or services purchased for consideration (personal use, not commercial resale)
Deficiency in service, defective product, or misleading advertisement
Dispute brought within limitation period of 2 years from date on which cause of action arose

procedural_steps.title: Collate Contemporaneous Evidence
procedural_steps.description: Preserve all invoices, proof of payment, warranty cards, delivery notes, and digital customer support tickets/chats.
evidence_required: Email / Chat history with customer care

procedural_steps.title: Pre-Litigation Written Notice to Trader / Manufacturer
procedural_steps.description: Serve a formal grievance notice demanding repair, replacement, or refund with compensation for harassment within 15 days.

procedural_steps.title: Lodge Pre-Litigation Grievance on National Consumer Helpline (NCH)
procedural_steps.description: Register complaint on consumerhelpline.gov.in or dial 1915. NCH facilitates direct conciliation with registered convergent companies without court fees.

procedural_steps.title: File Formal Consumer Complaint (e-Daakhil / District Commission)
procedural_steps.statutory_deadline: Within 2 years from date of cause of action (Section 69)
procedural_steps.description: File online via edaakhil.nic.in or physically at District Consumer Commission where you reside. No court fee for claims up to ₹5 lakh.
evidence_required: Complaint petition with index and synopsis

statutory_relief: Removal of defect, replacement of goods, refund of price paid, compensation for injury/harassment, and punitive damages.
forum: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (claims up to ₹50 Lakh)

title: Cyber Financial Fraud & Phishing Recovery (IT Act, 2000 & BNS, 2023)
statutory_prerequisites: Unauthorized debit or digital financial loss without voluntary informed consent
Prompt reporting to financial institutions to trigger RBI limited liability guidelines

procedural_steps.title: Immediate Golden Hour Emergency Call to 1930
procedural_steps.statutory_deadline: Within 2 to 4 hours of unauthorized transaction
procedural_steps.description: Dial National Cyber Financial Fraud Helpline 1930 immediately. Operator inputs transaction details into the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) to freeze the transaction in transit across banking APIs.
evidence_required: Sender and beneficiary bank account details

procedural_steps.title: Notify Bank to Block Accounts / Enforce RBI Zero-Liability
procedural_steps.description: Formally inform the bank branch and grievance officer in writing/email. Under RBI Circular RBI/2017-18/15, customer liability is zero if unauthorized electronic transaction is reported within three working days.
evidence_required: Bank account statement showing unauthorized debit

procedural_steps.title: Register Detailed Complaint on National Cyber Crime Portal
procedural_steps.description: File complaint at cybercrime.gov.in. System generates an official Acknowledgement Number necessary for police station FIR registration.
evidence_required: Screenshots of phishing URL, fake app, WhatsApp chat, or fake caller ID

procedural_steps.title: Lodge Zero-FIR / Regular FIR at Cyber Police Station
procedural_steps.description: Visit local Cyber Crime Police Station or nearest police station. Section 173(1) BNSS mandates immediate Zero-FIR registration for cognizable cyber fraud.

statutory_relief: Inter-bank fund freeze and restitution; criminal prosecution under Sections 66C/66D IT Act (up to 3 years imprisonment) and Section 318 BNS (cheating).
forum: Cyber Police Station / Magistrate Court / Adjudicating Officer under Section 46 IT Act

title: Security Deposit Recovery & Unlawful Eviction (Transfer of Property Act, 1882)
statutory_prerequisites: Lawful tenancy established through written lease agreement or rent receipts
Premises vacated in accordance with agreed notice period or statutory notice
Keys handed over or tendered in writing

procedural_steps.title: Document Handover Condition and Key Return
procedural_steps.description: Photograph/videotape all rooms, fixtures, and utility meters. Obtain signed handover inspection slip or send recorded delivery email confirming key return.
evidence_required: Key receipt or written intimation of key dispatch

procedural_steps.title: Serve Formal Statutory Legal Demand Notice
procedural_steps.statutory_deadline: Upon refusal or after agreed refund window (typically 7-15 days)
procedural_steps.description: Send formal legal notice demanding refund of undisputed security deposit within 15 days, specifying interest at 12-18% per annum from date of vacation.
evidence_required: Speed Post receipt and India Post delivery tracking record

procedural_steps.title: Approach Rent Authority / Consumer Commission / Civil Court
procedural_steps.statutory_deadline: Within 3 years limitation period for money recovery
procedural_steps.description: Depending on State Tenancy Act: file application before local Rent Authority / Rent Tribunal; or District Consumer Commission (if commercial landlord/co-living entity); or summary suit under Order XXXVII CPC for debt recovery.

statutory_relief: Full refund of deposit with statutory interest; damages for wrongful retention; injunctive relief against illegal dispossession.
forum: Rent Controller / Tribunal or Civil Court or Consumer Commission
